Sorry for skipping too many lines.

The official ruling is (item 5, DTR 11/9/95):

Call a vote with a Political Action card or as allowed by a card in play.
Have the vote pass.

Second Minion plays Charming Lobby. If unblocked, the next vote is
successful. Gain two Votes if superior.

Third Minion calls a vote with a Political Action card or as allowed
by a card in play. If unblocked, this vote passes automatically.

When do you cast those two votes? You can't use them during the first
vote, because you can't play the card then. You could use
them during the second vote, but that's a waste of time (if even allowed)
because the vote will pass automatically.

sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu (L. Scott Johnson) writes:

>The official ruling is (item 5, DTR 11/9/95):
>Call a vote with a Political Action card or as allowed by a card in play.

>Third Minion calls a vote with a Political Action card or as allowed

This is weird. The card is an action card and says "Call a vote...".
This means that you call a vote, doesn't it? I don't see why you
should have an additional card that allows you to call an additional
vote, or an additional vampire. CL says that you can call a vote, why
should you need an extra card? And if you have superior presence, you
gain 2 votes during THIS vote. So basically you vote whether the next
vote passes automatically.

CL vote is not a political vote, so you can't use cards that say "Only
usable during political actions". And if you only have one vamp left,
then the next vote that somebody calls (with a card or some other way)
passes automatically.

>>Third Minion calls a vote with a Political Action card or as allowed
>>by a card in play. If unblocked, this vote passes automatically.

>Did they really make such a hash of this card? "Calling a vote" means a
>vote happens. Playing a vote card to call a vote is a political action.
>The first is not an action and cannot be blocked (a diablerie vote is an
>example). The second is an action and can be blocked.

True. And yes, they really did a bad hack job on this card.

>Charming lobby is an action. If it succeed, its effects should take place
>(that IS how actions work, isn't it?) The result says "Call a vote", so
>you pick a subject and terms (I presume by playing the appropriate card)
>and the vampire Congress is in session. It doesn't say "Attempt to call a
>vote" or "Take a political action". Note the difference from Cryptic
>Rider, which says "The next vote you call this turn passes automatically."
> That doesn't call the vote for you.

That's the best way to play. However, a strict reading of the card is that
you are calling a vote, the terms of which are that the next vote will pass.

1. Vampire A performs a Charming Lobby. (no one blocks).
2. Vote. (A gets two votes if he has superior presence).
3. If the vote succeeds, the only effect is that the next vote called
will succeed.

>If calling a vote requires a vampire take an action, that would have to
>apply to bloodhunts too, which is obviously not the case.

If you mean that the Lobby allows you to call a vote (rather than having
to rely on PA cards), then I agree wholeheartedly.

>The 2 extra votes are real simple to interpret this way - there's a vote
>going on due to the Charming Lobby.

Yes, but it's still up to interpretation whether the vote is simply to
pass the next vote, or whether an additional PA can be used.

L. Scott

In article <3iiuse$2...@hermes.louisville.edu>, "James R. McClure Jr." <jrmc...@ulkyvm.louisville.edu> says:
>Protracted Investment: it is more effective than Shortterm Investment, gain
>of 3 (net) [PI] vs. gain of 2 (net) [SI]. If you have several PIs in your
>library, you can afford to use fewer Master cards, so you can concentrate on
>whatever else you deck is supposed to be good at (more skill/vote/weapon cards).

Good argument I agree with all of your points except the above one.
A [PI] gets me a net of 3 in 7 turns. 2 [SI]'s played on consecutive turns
will get you a net of 4 blood in 5 turns. Or look at it this way:
A [PI] gets you 6 for 3 or a 100% return on investment (RoI) in 7 turns.
A [SI] gets you 3 for 1 or a 200% (RoI) in 4 turns.
As you can see you get more bang for your buck from [SI]'s and you do not
have to tie up as much of your very precious blood resources to use [SI]'s

I freely admit that [PI]'s have a very definite use when you are really
tight on deck space and need every card slot you can squeeze out. But in
general I have to say that [SI]'s are way more useful and _effective_ than
[PI]'s

Do you think it would be fair to lower the cost of [PI] to 2 blood or
leave the cost at 3 blood and raise the return to 8 or 9 total ( 5 or 6
profit)? Or maybe leave [PI] like it is and allow you take 2 blood per
turn off of it?

Chris

Messages.Author: Bob Ellison
Messages.Body:
> Does Anson give you 2 master phases or just let you play 2 master cards
> each master phase?

Anson (or Rumors of Gehenna) gives you two master "actions". A master
"action" is the equivalent of playing one master card.

With Anson out, you can play two master cards, or play a master card and
take a blood off an investment, or take two blood off an investment (or
one blood each off of two investments). You cannot (for example) use
a Blood Doll to move two blood to a vampire.

And if you play an Out-of-turn Master, you lose your entire next Master
Phase. If you have Anson out, that means that you sacrifice *both*
master actions.

papillo the succinct

>for mundane actions. Note: no bleeding allowed. Have fun!

Aggravated damage would normally be used to burn a vampire whenever
possible, so it's not really a counter. It's tough to burn a vampire with
aggro under any circumstances, even if he's a wimp. Yes, everybody can
dream up "carefully reduce him to 0 blood and then flamethrower" scenarios
but if your opponent is a good player he will interfere with your
necessarily elaborate plans.

Minor boon is a very inadequate counter. First, it costs more (an entire
master phase) than the card it counters does (a master card play). This
is particularly disadvantageous in a multiplayer game (all other players
gain). Second, the Fame is still around and there are other good ways to
get to torpor (ever seen a Talbot's Chainsaw Fame deck? How about
intercept with Dawn Op or Burst of Sunlight or Trap?) Third, Minor Boon
is not a generally useful card so you can't afford to stick it in your
deck just in case you're prey for a Fame deck.
